solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Talk about deerstalker perhaps

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a deerstalker is one kind of hat, the 'perhaps' marking it as an example

explanation.surface: Someone discusses a deerstalker, perhaps the famous detective's headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: A deerstalker is a peaked tweed cap with ear flaps, the kind Sherlock Holmes is drawn wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual conversation is a synonym for informal talk, both as noun and verb.

clue.text: Doctor seen in outdoor clothing meeting worker and fighter

indicators.note: seen in means the doctor appears inside the garment

parts.note: a coat is worn outdoors
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A doctor in an overcoat meets a labourer and a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' puts the doctor inside the coat; 'meeting' and 'and' are just joins, with the definition at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engaged in fighting, as in a war, is a fighter or soldier.

clue.text: Found the total made sense

definitions.meaning: summed the figures to reach an overall amount
was logical or consistent, as in 'the story never quite' did so

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means summed numbers, and figuratively was coherent or plausible.

clue.text: Become gradually less light

definitions.meaning: to narrow or diminish bit by bit, as a spire does or as support for a policy may
a slender candle or wick used to carry a flame from a fire to a lamp

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to dwindle gradually; the noun is a thin candle used for lighting.

clue.text: African republic twinned with Bath — image that's surreal

indicators.note: surreal means dreamlike and distorted, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An African nation is twinned with the English spa city of Bath, a surreal picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twinned with' is just a link; 'that's surreal' rearranges BATHIMAGE. Bath is a Georgian spa city in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: The small West African country along the river of that name is a republic.

clue.text: Victoria paid for headlong plunge

parts.note: the Victoria is a popular English variety of plum
to have met a bill is to have paid it

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria funded a dramatic fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like the queen or the London station, but is a variety of plum.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep rapid fall, as of a share price, is a sudden steep drop.

clue.text: Animal with another animal on American railroad

parts.note: a rat is an animal
an el is an elevated railway in American cities such as Chicago

explanation.surface: One creature rides with another on a US railway.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first word; 'with' simply joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey badger of Africa and Asia is a burrowing carnivorous mammal.

clue.text: Commander's rejected story

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for the commander's is read backwards

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander; with the possessive it gives AGAS

explanation.surface: A commander's tale has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is an Ottoman commander or chief officer, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrative, originally an Icelandic heroic tale, is a kind of story.

clue.text: Hit no longer available, being deleted

parts.note: struck means hit
a dish that is off the menu is no longer available

explanation.surface: A hit record is withdrawn and erased from the catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A name removed from a register, as a doctor from the medical roll, has been erased.

clue.text: Sea where girl and I may find shelter

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A lake where a young woman and the speaker might take refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: The freshwater lake in northern Israel is traditionally called a sea in the Bible.

clue.text: Bats flutter maybe, flapping about in opera

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, so it means mad

indicators.note: flapping about suggests wings beating chaotically, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bats possibly flutter, flapping around inside an opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the flying creatures but is slang for crazy, and 'flapping about' gives AMEBUTTERFLY; the bats are not part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's tragic Japanese-set work is a famous example of an opera.

clue.text: Read an adaptation for this lady!

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks material into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to read an adapted text aimed at a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adaptation' turns READAN into the name; the exclamation mark tells you the definition is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so it can stand for some lady being referred to.

clue.text: Spy translated clue for atomic group

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy has decoded a hint about a cluster of atoms.
explanation.walkthrough: In spy fiction a mole is an agent buried deep inside a rival organisation; 'translated' gives CULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemically, a bonded cluster of atoms forms the smallest unit of a compound.

clue.text: Characters in order of appearance

parts.note: reads like a theatre programme listing the cast, but describes letters set out in their fixed sequence

explanation.definitionFit: The set of letters of a language, given in their standard sequence from A onwards.

clue.text: Silence young dog with savoury doughnut

parts.note: hush means silence
a puppy is a young dog

explanation.surface: Quieten the puppy by offering it a tasty fried snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last two words; 'with' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-fried ball of cornmeal batter from the American South, a savoury fritter.

clue.text: Crooked trefoil I left produces small bloomer

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
left means departed, so the I is taken away from the word

explanation.surface: A bent clover-leaf shape that someone has abandoned produces a little mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' removes I from TREFOIL to leave TREFOL, and 'Crooked' rearranges that. 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flowering thing.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the tiny flowers making up a composite head, so a small flowering part.

clue.text: Entertainment for clubbers' night on the tiles?

definitions.text: Entertainment for clubbers' night on the tiles?

parts.words: Entertainment for clubbers' night on the tiles?
parts.note: a night on the tiles is a night out, but literally it is a display performed on the tiled ground of a nightclub

explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret performed in a nightclub on the dancing area rather than a raised stage.

clue.text: One of a band of elephants?

definitions.text: One of a band of elephants?

parts.words: One of a band of elephants?
parts.note: elephants make a trumpeting noise, so a member of their imaginary brass band would play the horn

explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays the brass horn, and also anything that trumpets, like a bull elephant.

clue.text: Mend a shirt for this lady!

indicators.note: to mend is to repair or rework something, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to repair a shirt for a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mend' rearranges ASHIRT into the name; the exclamation mark points to a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so it can stand for some lady being referred to.

clue.text: Coming to a similar conclusion, we hear

definitions.text: Coming to a similar conclusion, we hear

parts.words: Coming to a similar conclusion, we hear
parts.note: reads like people agreeing, but describes words whose endings sound alike to the ear

explanation.definitionFit: Words that share their final sounds, as in verse, end alike when heard.

clue.text: Four repeatedly redesigned fussy decoration

indicators.note: redesigned means given a new layout, so the doubled letters are rearranged
repeatedly says the word is used twice over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A design of four motifs reworked again and again into something over-ornate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles FOUR to FOURFOUR, and 'redesigned' rearranges each into FROU.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate frills and ornamentation on clothing are an over-elaborate trim.

clue.text: Agitated by improper fraction, nothing less

indicators.note: improper, as in an improper fraction, means wrongly arranged, so the letters are reshuffled
less means minus, so the letter for nothing is removed

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone is flustered by a top-heavy fraction with zero taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing less' removes O from FRACTION to leave FRACTIN, and 'improper' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildly anxious or distraught, the state of someone in a panic.

clue.text: Residence of minister seized from director? Yes

indicators.note: seized from means the letters are grabbed out of the middle of the words

explanation.surface: A minister's home has been confiscated from a director, who confirms it.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles the question mark: diRECTOR? Yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The house provided for a parish rector, a Church of England clergyman.

clue.text: Conferences required when centre of Syria is occupied by politicians accepting nothing

indicators.note: centre of points to the middle letter of the country's name
is occupied by means that middle letter is displaced by an invading group
accepting means the politicians take in the next piece

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament, i.e. politicians
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Peace talks are needed when politicians who accept nothing seize the heart of Syria.
explanation.walkthrough: MPS takes in O to give MPOS, which replaces the R at the centre of SYRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal meetings for discussion of a subject, the plural of a Greek-derived word for a gathering.

clue.text: Therefore friar may be cut off in old city

parts.note: so means therefore

indicators.note: cut off means the end is lopped from the word for a friar

parts.note: a Dominican is a friar of the order founded by St Dominic

explanation.surface: So a friar could be excluded from an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: DOMINICAN loses its tail to leave DOM, also the title given to some monks.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed with Gomorrah was an ancient settlement.

clue.text: Military policeman cut down while arresting District Commissioner

indicators.note: while arresting means the first word holds the abbreviation inside it, like a captor

parts.note: to reap is to cut down a crop
DC is the standard abbreviation for District Commissioner

explanation.surface: A military policeman is cut down as he arrests a colonial official.
explanation.walkthrough: Military police in the British Army wear red-topped caps, hence the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a member of the Royal Military Police, from their red cap covers.

clue.text: Just beaten by top path, I stepped a different way

indicators.note: a different way means the letters are taken in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Narrowly defeated because I took a different route along the top path.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the start; 'by' links it to fodder TOPPATHISTEPPED, which 'a different way' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from racing for losing at the very last moment, defeated by a narrow margin.

clue.text: Unfair, making regular visits to Burghley

indicators.note: regular visits suggests calling at every other letter of the place name

explanation.surface: Something unjust happens on repeated trips to a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: Burghley is an Elizabethan stately home in Lincolnshire; take its 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair can mean beautiful, so its opposite plays on the sense of unattractive.

clue.text: Many a bird call from this bird!

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many
caw is the cry of a crow or rook

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a bird whose call is loud and frequent.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brightly coloured parrot of Central and South America is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Dreadful sound made by colourful worker

indicators.note: sound says the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: dire means dreadful

explanation.surface: A painful noise comes from a vividly dressed labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who colours fabric is literally a worker in colour.
